subject: english-literature
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which two assessment objectives are assessed in Paper 1: Poetry and Modern Prose?
options: AO1 and AO2
AO3 and AO4
AO1 and AO3
AO2 and AO4
questions.explain: Paper 1 assesses AO1 (knowledge, understanding and personal response) and AO2 (analysis of language, form and structure).

questions.q: What does AO2 require candidates to do?
options: Analyse the language, form and structure a writer uses to create meanings and effects, using subject terminology
Explore links and connections between different texts
Show understanding of the contexts in which texts were written
Summarise the plot of the text in their own words
questions.explain: AO2 focuses on analysing how writers use language, form and structure, supported by relevant subject terminology.

questions.q: Who wrote the anthology poem 'My Last Duchess'?
options: Robert Browning
Alfred Tennyson
John Keats
Carol Ann Duffy
questions.explain: 'My Last Duchess' is a dramatic monologue written by Robert Browning.

questions.q: The anthology poem 'If—' was written by which poet?
options: Rudyard Kipling
Dylan Thomas
Louis MacNeice
D H Lawrence
questions.explain: 'If—', a poem of paternal advice, was written by Rudyard Kipling.

questions.q: Who is the poet of 'Do not go gentle into that good night'?
options: Dylan Thomas
Christina Rossetti
William Shakespeare
Gabriel Okara
questions.explain: 'Do not go gentle into that good night' is a villanelle by Dylan Thomas addressed to his dying father.

questions.q: Which author wrote the modern prose set text 'Of Mice and Men'?
options: John Steinbeck
Harper Lee
Chinua Achebe
Meera Syal
questions.explain: 'Of Mice and Men' is a novella by John Steinbeck, one of the modern prose set texts.

questions.q: Which of these is a modern prose set text for this paper?
options: Things Fall Apart by Chinua Achebe
Great Expectations by Charles Dickens
Pride and Prejudice by Jane Austen
Frankenstein by Mary Shelley
questions.explain: 'Things Fall Apart' by Chinua Achebe is one of the studied modern prose set texts on the specification.

questions.q: Who wrote the anthology poem 'War Photographer'?
options: Carol Ann Duffy
Sujata Bhatt
Imtiaz Dharker
U A Fanthorpe
questions.explain: 'War Photographer' was written by Carol Ann Duffy and explores the detachment and suffering of documenting conflict.

questions.q: The form of 'Do not go gentle into that good night' is a villanelle. Which description fits a villanelle?
options: A 19-line poem of five tercets and a closing quatrain using two repeated refrains
A 14-line poem written in iambic pentameter
An unrhymed narrative poem of any length
A four-line stanza with an ABAB rhyme scheme
questions.explain: A villanelle has 19 lines arranged as five tercets and a quatrain, with two lines recurring as refrains.

questions.q: Which of the following best demonstrates an AO1 skill?
options: Giving an informed, critical personal response supported by references to the text
Naming the metrical pattern of a poem
Comparing the contexts of two different texts
Identifying sibilance in a single line
questions.explain: AO1 rewards close knowledge and an informed personal response supported by textual reference.

questions.q: 'My Last Duchess' is a dramatic monologue. What does this form mean?
options: A single speaker addresses a silent listener, unintentionally revealing his character
Two speakers debate an issue in alternating stanzas
A narrator tells a story about characters in the third person
A chorus comments on the action between scenes
questions.explain: In a dramatic monologue one speaker (the Duke) speaks to a silent listener, revealing more than he intends.

questions.q: What is the central concern of Imtiaz Dharker's 'Blessing'?
options: The value of water to a community suffering drought when a pipe bursts
A soldier's memories of a distant battlefield
A child's confusion about telling the time
A knight bewitched by a mysterious woman
questions.explain: 'Blessing' presents water as precious, celebrated by a poor community when a pipe bursts.

questions.q: The examination is 'closed book'. What does this mean for the Modern Prose section?
options: Candidates answer without the text in front of them and must rely on their own knowledge
Candidates may bring an annotated copy of the novel into the exam
Candidates are given extracts printed on the question paper only
Candidates choose their own text on the day of the exam
questions.explain: Closed book means students cannot use the text in the exam and must draw on remembered detail and quotation.

questions.q: What theme does Sujata Bhatt explore in 'Search For My Tongue'?
options: The tension and identity of living between two languages
The horror of nuclear war
The loss of childhood innocence in a game
A daughter's grief for her father
questions.explain: 'Search For My Tongue' explores bilingual identity and the fear of losing one's 'mother tongue'.

questions.q: Who is the speaker in Louis MacNeice's 'Prayer Before Birth'?
options: An unborn child fearful of the world it is about to enter
An elderly man reflecting on his life
A soldier writing home from war
A mother addressing her newborn baby
questions.explain: 'Prayer Before Birth' is voiced by an unborn child pleading for protection from the world's cruelties.

questions.q: AO2 asks students to use 'subject terminology'. Which of these is an example of appropriate subject terminology?
options: Enjambment
Paragraph
Synopsis
Chapter
questions.explain: Enjambment is a technical poetic term describing a sentence running over the line break, suitable for AO2 analysis.

questions.q: A student notes the repeated soft 's' sounds in the phrase 'the soft silence slips'. Which technique should they name?
options: Sibilance
Onomatopoeia
Assonance
Caesura
questions.explain: The repetition of 's' sounds is sibilance, which often creates a soft or hushed effect.

questions.q: Facing an unseen poem in the exam, which approach best satisfies AO1 and AO2?
options: Read the poem closely, then analyse how language, form and structure create meaning, supporting each point with quotation
Retell what happens in the poem line by line without comment
Describe the poet's biography and historical background in detail
Compare the poem to a novel studied for another paper
questions.explain: Unseen response rewards close reading plus analysis of method (AO2) and an evidenced personal response (AO1).

questions.q: A candidate writes: 'The metaphor comparing the guns to toys makes the violence seem casual.' Which objective does this most clearly demonstrate?
options: AO2, because it analyses a technique and its effect
AO1, because it gives biographical context
AO3, because it links two texts
AO4, because it discusses historical context
questions.explain: Identifying a device and explaining the effect it creates is exactly what AO2 rewards.

questions.q: In the line 'Stop! — I heard him call', the dash creates a distinct pause in the middle of the line. What is this technique called?
options: Caesura
Enjambment
Refrain
Stanza
questions.explain: A caesura is a deliberate pause within a line, often marked by punctuation such as a dash.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE English Literature (4ET1) specification; Paper 1: Poetry and Modern Prose
